s: Blackstone defined liberty of the press as freedom from prior restraints.
Prior restraints, whether court injunctions or administrative censorship, bear a "heavy presumption" against validity.
Licensing schemes must have narrow, objective, definite standards (Shuttlesworth v. Birmingham, 1969).
Content-based licensing requires procedural safeguards: a brief period before a judicial determination, prompt judicial review, and a burden on the censor (Freedman v. Maryland, 1965).
Permit fees may not vary with the anticipated hostility of the audience (Forsyth County v. Nationalist Movement, 1992).
